svg.title: Five Core Seats; Two Seats Added at Scale
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-five-to-seven-person-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Five Core Seats; Two Seats Added at Scale; subtitle: Conservative and Base: 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled: 3 FT + 4 C.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: FT means full-time employee; C means contractor seat with variable engagement hours. Each stage represents one seat, not one full-time equivalent. Seats six and seven exist only in the Scaled Small-Team scenario; headcount alone does not establish capacity.; caption: Canonical annual outcomes: Conservative $120,000 revenue at 15% equals $18,000 owner net; Base $560,000 at 22.5% equals $126,000; Scaled $1,000,000 at 30% equals $300,000. Recognized service fees remain the revenue basis in every scenario.; stages: label: Managing operator; value: Core seat one: full-time accountable lead; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own client selection, service pricing, conflict review, cash forecasting, and engagement scope. Approve pursuit capacity using actual hours and receivables rather than the nominal value of prospective client awards.; label: Bid operations manager; value: Core seat two: full-time workflow owner; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Maintain solicitation alerts, bid calendars, version control, amendment tracking, and submission receipts. Escalate missed client inputs early enough to withdraw or revise a pursuit without a defective submission.; label: Capture analyst; value: Core seat three: contracted research specialist; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Screen SAM.gov notices and municipal opportunities, map requirements to supplier capabilities, and maintain pursuit evidence. Distinguish public opportunity intelligence from protected procurement information.; label: Proposal specialist; value: Core seat four: contracted production specialist; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Assemble response matrices, edit client-provided technical content, and check required attachments. Record unresolved claims for client correction instead of inventing past performance or unsupported qualifications.; label: Supplier performance verifier; value: Core seat five: contracted delivery specialist; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Validate supplier commitments, lead times, workshare evidence, and delivery dependencies. Escalate supplier failure and substitution risk before the client commits to an unsupported performance schedule.; label: Client delivery lead; value: Scaled seat six: additional full-time employee; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Add in the Scaled scenario to manage service acceptance, renewals, and cross-client workload. The resulting employee count is three; preserve separation between client award administration and operator service billing.; label: Surge proposal specialist; value: Scaled seat seven: additional contracted specialist; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Add in the Scaled scenario for concurrent submission peaks and independent package checks. The resulting contractor count is four; schedule actual availability rather than assuming every contractor works full time.

rect.title: label: Managing operator; value: Core seat one: full-time accountable lead; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own client selection, service pricing, conflict review, cash forecasting, and engagement scope. Approve pursuit capacity using actual hours and receivables rather than the nominal value of prospective client awards.
